cases.heading: Inner Child Therapy
cases.owner_words: h2. a wow i can't believe i wrote tha... oh that was from GPT, i humanized it but didn't notice how jarring that last stupid sentence was
cases.owner_target: You can always slow down and look closer when it helps.
cases.baseline: Reparenting means consciously evolving and molding an Inner Adult inside you, comprising a loving Nurturer, a safe Adult Protector (hereafter just the Protector) and a wise Guide. This chosen Inner Adult super hero gets into a real, loving relationship with the little one you still carry. That grown-up notices the old patterns and practices better ways of responding. At first, it’s deliberate, even awkward. With time, the roles become second nature, so you spend less of your life managing yourself and more of it living with purpose, loving, relaxing, and playing.

cases.heading: If the Love Isn't Coming Yet
cases.owner_target: , and it isn't a test of whether you were loved enough
cases.baseline: Maybe just imagining a caring grown-up makes you feel more threatened, or lonelier. Lonelier is a strange one, with somebody right there. Then go smaller still, to the least cruel response a decent adult could offer your little one. It's scaffolding.

cases.heading: Not Every Hero Wears A Cape
cases.owner_target: Some of them are only one step anyway.
cases.baseline: Intentional, meaning you pick one of those acts and decide when you'll do it, and what the smallest first step is (like with the envelope). If it needs money or somebody's help, sort that out before the day, and if you'll have to tell someone something they won't like, say it out loud to yourself ahead of time. Then put yourself in their shoes to see how it sounds, and go back & forth like that a couple times until both sides feel good about it, or good enough, as long as what you needed to say is still in there.

cases.heading: Catch the Hook Before the Story Takes Over
cases.owner_words: h14 a it doesn't tell the reader the detective work can wait, that's what the prior sentence said..
cases.owner_target: You can figure that out later.
cases.baseline: Pema Chödrön calls the tightening and urge you get before the story has finished forming "shenpa," and she says "hooked" is a more descriptive translation than the usual "attachment." You might notice the hook before you have any clue what part of you is doing the hooking. Or you might notice it embarrassingly late. The jaw and stomach are already tight, and/or half the text is written, and then suddenly it dawns on you: you're supposed to be observing yourself. 😀 Maybe forget the parts detective work for a minute.

cases.heading: Use Childhood Photographs Gently
cases.baseline: While you look, notice what your body does and what feelings or urges show up. Is there something that younger you seems to want you to understand? Some of it you'll remember yourself, and some of it you might even glean from talking to family/friends from then ("You hated that coat"). It might just be an inference you're guessing from the picture, or perhaps it triggers an image or a dream. Or just nothing comes up. Ask what your little one needs from you now, and do a bit of it.

edits.old: an inference you're guessing from the picture
edits.new: a guess you're making from the picture
edits.why: "inference you're guessing" is redundant, since an inference is already a guess. This keeps the same tentative certainty in plainer wording.

And any predisposition toward mania or psychosis is a warning sign too, whether it's family history, a bad environment or a bad mindset. These are just caution signs, and when you see them, you take more precautions of every kind. You have to figure out what they mean for you, and if you can't, get help from trusted advisors.

cases.heading: When the Adult Voice Feels Fake
cases.owner_target: They can feel totally real, but that alone doesn't prove they happened.
cases.baseline: For some people it only stops feeling fake in an altered state, like on MDMA or deep in meditation. All of a sudden your little one is right there! Oh my gosh! And the love or grief that sounded like therapy talk is just obvious. Old memories might come up too. They can feel totally real, but that alone doesn't prove they happened. I'd still hang on to what you felt, even once it's gone, and try to bring a little of it into your normal life.
